caption: The video captures a shallow woodland stream in autumn, framed by a dense tangle of bare gray twigs and a few scattered green leaves. A weathered log lies diagonally across the left bank, while moss-covered boulders line the right. At the center, water already tumbles continuously over a cluster of dark rocks. Its frothy white plume churns and reforms without pause as it feeds a foaming pool at the bottom edge. Behind a horizontal fallen branch in the mid-ground, a second, gentler cascade spills over submerged stones. The aerated surface there likewise shifts in shape and brightness. The solid elements—the log, rocks, branches, and leaves—hold fixed screen positions throughout, and the camera angle does not change. Only the moving water reveals the passage of time, its turbulent foam breaking and reknitting over the boulders in an unbroken flow that is underway at the start and still underway at the close.
relations: Water flowing over the central rock cluster generates a white frothy plume that continuously churns and reforms.
The second cascade behind the fallen branch spills over submerged stones, its aerated surface shifting shape and brightness.
The log, rocks, branches, and leaves remain fixed in screen position while only the water moves.
The camera angle stays constant, so the unbroken flow of foam breaking and reknitting reveals the passage of time.
